product.seoTitle: SpiderWire Ultracast 8 lb Diameter & Capacity Guide | ReelCalc
product.metaDescription: Plan an 8 lb SpiderWire Ultracast Inshore Camo setup using its labeled diameter and 164-yard package. Estimate reel capacity, working braid and mono backing.
product.quickSummary: Ultracast is an eight-fiber PE braid. This guide is limited to the labeled 8 lb Inshore Camo package, not the full Ultracast range. Its 164-yard spool gives you a defined amount of working braid to plan around; a large capacity estimate does not mean you need to fill the entire reel with it.
product.suitabilityTitle: A thin working line, with a specific label
product.suitabilitySummary: Consider this 8 lb variant only where the rod, lure and fishing conditions suit light braid. A spinning-reel setup with a deliberately chosen working length is a sensible planning example. Inshore Camo is a color name, not proof that this strength suits every inshore fishery. The unusually small published diameter makes backing calculations sensitive to the label and to real-world packing, so finish by checking the reel's recommended fill level.
strengthGuide: Match the 8 lb test rating to the rod, lure and likely loads first. Do not select it solely because the small published diameter produces a large capacity estimate.
The package also prints a maximum-break figure. That is a different label field, not a substitute for the 8 lb test rating and not an instruction to use a heavier drag setting.
Only this labeled variant is charted here. Use separately verified data for stronger Ultracast, another color formulation, or the older Ultimate Braid and Invisibraid products.
product.bestFit: A light spinning setup where the angler has already selected 8 lb braid and wants a measured working section over backing. Keep enough reserve for the longest cast, fish runs and line removed through use.
product.tradeoffTitle: Published diameter is not a fill guarantee
product.tradeoff: Braid can pack differently with tension and spool geometry. With such a small listed diameter, an apparent surplus of reel capacity should be handled with a backing plan, not a promise that an exact calculated length will fit in practice.
product.reviewNote: This is a specification-based guide. No casting-distance, abrasion or handling performance was independently tested.
product.chartNote: One verified package only: 8 lb Inshore Camo, labeled 164 yd / 150 m. Other Ultracast strengths are intentionally absent because their physical diameters and matching packages were not verified from the current manufacturer's evidence.

spoolingGuide.title: Budget from the 164-yard package
spoolingGuide.text: Start with your required working length, leaving room for trimming and future losses. The examples use 125 or 150 yards from one package, not a promise that either length suits every fishery.

spoolingGuide.title: Fill the remaining volume underneath
spoolingGuide.text: Choose the exact reel before estimating mono backing. Follow its instructions for attaching braid; a smooth arbor may need an approved anti-slip attachment or a mono base. Backing length is a volume calculation, not a matching pound-test rule.

spoolingGuide.title: Treat the leader separately
spoolingGuide.text: Choose any lure-end leader for the presentation and contact hazards. It is not the backing beneath the braid, and its test rating need not copy the braid label. A long topshot needs a separate allowance for spool space.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the final fill
spoolingGuide.text: Wind with controlled, even tension and stop at the reel manufacturer's specified clearance. Correct the backing amount if the actual fill differs from the estimate; do not force all the planned line onto an overfull spool.

faqs.question: Why can the calculated capacity look unusually large?
faqs.answer: The package lists a very small diameter. Capacity estimates depend strongly on that input, while actual braid packing also depends on winding tension and spool shape. Treat the result as a planning estimate and verify the final fill.

product.quickSummary: This guide covers SpiderWire Ultracast Ultimate Mono's 2018 US published Clear specifications only. It is the copolymer mono family, not Ultracast Braid or Fluoro-Braid. product.suitabilityTitle: A mono plan with an edition-specific diameter
product.suitabilitySummary: Ultimate Mono was positioned around a thinner, lower-stretch mono concept. Before using these historical inputs for a package in hand, check that its identity and labeling match the 2018 scope.
strengthGuide: The 4-8 lb rows are the light end of the 2018 table. Choose them only where the tackle and conditions suit their test ratings; extra spool capacity is not a substitute for adequate strength.
The 10,12,15 and 17 lb entries use the same published filler length in this edition, but their different diameters still produce different reel capacities.
The 20 lb entry is both thicker and supplied in a shorter filler package. Plan its working reserve independently rather than assuming one package fills every reel.
Keep the later 14 lb entry out of this chart. A changed strength label and a later diameter typo cannot be resolved by joining rows from different editions.

spoolingGuide.title: Identify Ultimate Mono first

spoolingGuide.title: Start with a full mono fill
spoolingGuide.text: A separate anti-slip backing layer is not required for the reason it may be used beneath braid. If you choose a shorter fresh mono section over backing, leave sufficient reserve above the connection.

spoolingGuide.title: Confirm the final level

product.metaDescription: Compare Stren Original's published 2016 US diameters, estimate reel capacity and plan a mono fill using the strength-specific archived filler-spool lengths.
product.quickSummary: Stren Original is the purple-package monofilament family, distinct from MagnaThin, Crappie Mono and High Impact. This guide uses the manufacturer's 2016 US filler chart. It is a dated specification reference, not a claim that every historical package remains available today.
product.suitabilityTitle: A full mono fill with clear package limits
product.suitabilitySummary: Original gives anglers a broad range of mono diameters to compare for a spinning or casting setup. Start with the rod, lure and cover, then check the exact diameter against the reel. A reel labeled for 10 lb line does not require 10 lb Original. The upper end of the range occupies substantially more space, and a smaller retail package at the heavier strengths does not imply a smaller reel is suitable.
strengthGuide: The 4-8 lb entries provide the light end of this archived range. Select them for an appropriate light-line setup, not simply to maximize the number of yards on a spool.
Compare the 10-17 lb choices by diameter as well as test. The reel's volume, rod limits, casting load and contact with cover all matter; capacity alone cannot choose strength.
The 20-30 lb entries need equipment suited to thicker mono. Keep their changing filler lengths separate from the thinner strengths rather than assuming every purple package contains the same yardage.

spoolingGuide.title: Use a full mono fill as the starting point
spoolingGuide.text: Original can be the entire line on the reel. A separate anti-slip mono layer is not needed beneath another mono just because braid setups sometimes use one. Follow the reel's attachment and fill instructions.

spoolingGuide.title: Calculate from the selected package
spoolingGuide.text: The archived filler table lists 330 yards through 17 lb, then 300, 250 and 220 yards at 20, 25 and 30 lb. Plan a full fill or multiple smaller fills from the correct entry, allowing for trimming.

spoolingGuide.title: Use backing only with a purpose
spoolingGuide.text: A fresh working section over sound backing can reduce replacement line use, but it introduces a connection. Keep that knot below the longest expected cast and the reserve needed for fish runs.

product.suitabilityTitle: Compare the diameter, not just the test label
product.suitabilitySummary: MagnaThin is worth considering when you want a mono mainline and spool space matters. Its smaller published sizes can change a fill plan appreciably, but extra capacity is not itself a reason to choose lighter line. Match strength to the rod, lure and cover before comparing reels. strengthGuide: The 4-10 lb rows are the thinner part of this chart. They give you concrete diameter inputs for a light-line plan; the lowest number is not automatically the best choice for a compact reel.

The 20 and 30 lb entries increase spool-volume demand substantially. Pick the rod and reel for the fishing load, then check whether the package provides your required working length.

spoolingGuide.title: Finish by the spool lip

product.suitabilitySummary: Crappie Mono provides light strengths to consider for small-lure and panfish setups. Its product name does not mean one strength suits every crappie technique: heavier rigs and contact with cover can change the requirement. Choose the rod, rig and working reserve first. strengthGuide: Use 2 lb only where the rod, drag, rig and contact hazards suit very light line. Extra capacity does not compensate for an unsuitable strength.
The 4 and 6 lb entries are distinct physical sizes, not interchangeable copies of Stren Original. Select the exact family before relying on a reel-fill estimate.

The verified 8 and 10 lb rows extend beyond the earlier database inventory. They come from this same edition's table, not interpolation. Decide whether the heavier size suits the fishing rather than selecting it simply to consume more of the package.

spoolingGuide.title: Use the 200-yard package as a budget
spoolingGuide.text: The reviewed table uses 200-yard filler packages across its listed strengths. On a compact reel that may leave line for another partial fill; on a deeper reel it may fall short of a complete fill.
